document.abstract: Convergence of technologies and increasing globalisation are driving change in education as in broadcasting. Changes too in the process of specifying courses means that course distinguishing features are defined by the Australian Qualifications Framework, and in the VET sector course outcomes are defined by training packages driven by industry standards. The old “content-driven” model of course definition no longer applies. The broadcast industry can influence training in the new system by becoming involved in training package development through relevant Industry Training Boards, by participating in the development of resources, or by supporting flexible delivery including workplace delivery. It can also customise courses developed for other relevant industry sectors. While change is occurring, the development of resources is the responsibility of providers: it is no longer being publicly funded. Development needs industry support if it is to progress faster than it currently is. Assistance in developing resources using the expertise of broadcasters would bring the joint benefit of ensuring relevant content and speeding global access.

authors.bio: Rodney qualified as an engineer from RMIT in 1977 after studying part time while working in military communications and computing. After taking up teaching he developed courses in electronics and audio technology and taught audio and television production alongside general electronics and communications subjects. For more than two decades he has been directly involved in curriculum development in the areas of electronics, communications, broadcasting and telecommunications. Recent work includes a specialist conversion course in Telecommunications in conjunction with Telstra. In addition to the engineering qualification Rodney holds several qualifications in education including a Master of Education degree. Rodney is a member of the SMPTE.
